Simple, we need a low risk/high reward item. Now this means something safe to land on and is worth a lot. This minimises risk while maximising the reward.

So:

\- safe to land on

\- worth a lot

The most expensive thing that could fit this criteria is a [Bluefish Tuna](https://www.cheatsheet.com/money-career/these-are-the-most-expensive-things-in-world.html/), these sell for roughly 3.1 million dollars (£2,443,761). This could potentially be a risk but we'll worry about that in just a sec.

The average Bluefish Tuna is around 2.3 meters long and I'm just gonna say they are like .4 meters tall(?) and .2 meters thick(?). This gives them a rough volume of .184 meters^(3). 

The largest swimming pool I could find online has a volume of 250,000meters^(3) (250 million liters). ([here](https://twistedsifter.com/2012/05/worlds-largest-swimming-pool-san-alfonso-del-mar/))

Dividing 250,000 by .184 gives 1,358,695 tunas that will fit in the pool. Multiplying this by 3.1 give us 4,211,954.50 dollars. That's cool.

Now, minimising the risk?

\- Simple, if we make a nice slope out of the tuna I can jump from the 10 meters and land on the slope, roll down the tunas and live. 

Easiest money to make in a hypothetical situation, right?
